speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds distressing. To understand what's happening, have you experienced any warning signs like a strange smell, a rising feeling in your stomach, or unusual sensations right before becoming unresponsive?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That "muddy taste" is a classic aura; could you or the brother observe any rhythmic jerking, bicycling motions of the hands, or lip smacking during the staring spells? Also, has there been any recent illness, fever, or head trauma?

REQUEST TEST: EEG (Electroencephalogram)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history. No prior seizures or neurological evaluations. Social history: Enrolled in second grade. Lives with parents and one sibling. No reported use of medications or exposure to toxins.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, headache, visual or auditory disturbances, weakness, or other systemic symptoms. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Childhood Absence Epilepsy (specifically focal impaired awareness seizures with automatisms, likely evolving from a focal onset given the aura and hand gestures).
